data.title: Afghanistan says deadly Pakistani strikes hit Helmand
data.description: KABUL — The Pakistani military launched rare deadly strikes on Afghanistan's Helmand province on Thursday, the Taliban government and residents told Agence France-Presse ( AFP ).

data.title: Kremlin critic, chess legend Kasparov says US intelligence warned life 'in danger'
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Kremlin critic and chess legend Garry Kasparov said Thursday that US and Lithuanian security services had told him and his ally that their lives were in danger and urged them to take security precautions.

data.title: Indian pilot hailed as ‘hero’ after cockpit struggle
data.description: MUMBAI — Indian pilot Smit Machchhar was hailed as a "hero" on Thursday after fighting to retain control of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight when his co-pilot attacked him, leaving him wounded but helping avert disaster.

data.title: Plastic treaty talks chair sees deal possible in March
data.description: Countries negotiating a world-first treaty to limit plastic pollution are less divided than before and a deal could be agreed in March, the diplomat chairing the talks told Agence France-Presse ( AFP ) on Thursday.

data.title: US woman survives lethal-drug execution attempt
data.description: Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a schoolmate three decades ago, survived an attempt to execute her by means of lethal injection late on Wednesday, foiling the first attempt to put a woman to death in Tennessee for two centuries.

data.title: Man City scandal could taint Premier League brand
data.description: MANCHESTER, England - The Premier League has won a lengthy legal battle with Manchester City over financial impropriety, but the consequences could leave lasting damage for a league that has long since become the envy of world football.

data.title: Japan tightens permanent residency rules for foreigners
data.description: TOKYO - Japan has toughened requirements for foreigners wanting to obtain permanent residency, as part of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s push to tighten immigration controls.

data.title: Dozens wounded as French school protests escalate
data.description: PARIS - French security forces on Wednesday detained over 600 people while dozens of police and gendarmes were wounded as protests that have seen blockades of high schools and violent clashes escalated, the interior minister said.

data.title: EU seeking better ways to manage deportations
data.description: BRUSSELS - The European Union will discuss further ways to boost migrant deportations on Thursday, as a group of nations forges ahead with divisive plans to send failed asylum-seekers to return centres outside the bloc.

data.title: Hundreds held, dozens wounded as French school protests escalate
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French security forces on Wednesday detained over 600 people while dozens of police and gendarmes were wounded as protests that have seen blockades of high schools and violent clashes escalated, the interior minister said.

data.title: 'Catastrophic': Swiss glaciers lose fifth of mass in five years
data.description: LES DIABLERETS (SWITZERLAND) - Switzerland's glaciers, which are disproportionately impacted by climate change, have lost nearly 20 percent of their mass in five years, experts said Thursday, with 2026 registering the second-biggest melt on record.

data.title: US government's new AI chatbot pulls back from debunking Trump
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump unveiled what he called a "damn good" AI chatbot, but it quickly drew attention for contradicting some of his contentious political claims.

data.title: Google restricts access to new AI model over safety concerns
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - Google on Wednesday said it would withhold its most powerful artificial intelligence model from the public for now, releasing Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts to avoid misuse by hackers.

data.title: Panic, anger, tears: Evan Gershkovich's uneasy journey after Russian jail
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US journalist Evan Gershkovich spent nearly 500 days in a tiny Russian jail cell. When he was finally set free two years ago as part of an extraordinary multi-country prisoner swap, it took him almost as long to heal.

data.title: Hegseth says US cut number of generals, admirals by 20%
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Wednesday that the United States has slashed the number of its generals and admirals by 20 percent, in a move he said is aimed at "accountability."

data.title: UK PM says 'strong indications' Iran involved in airbase incident
data.description: LONDON - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Wednesday said there were "strong indications" Iran was involved in suspicious activity at a UK airbase that triggered a major security incident this weekend.

data.title: Israelis march between once-closed West Bank settlements
data.description: KADIM (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Hundreds of Israelis marched Wednesday between newly rebuilt settlements in the northern West Bank to celebrate a Jewish holiday, a symbolic show of their return to an area until recently almost fully Palestinian.

data.title: Oil companies close in on Venezuela despite hurdles
data.description: CARACAS - Foreign oil companies scrambled for a slice of Venezuela's crude at an oil summit in Caracas this week despite years of sanctions, underinvestment and mismanagement that have crippled the once booming industry.

data.title: Court halts Tennessee's first execution of woman in 200 years
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - A US court on Wednesday halted the lethal injection of a 50-year-old female killer that would have been Tennessee's first execution of a woman in more than 200 years.

data.title: France in talks with UK to end 2025 migrant accord: ministry
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France is in discussions with the UK on ending a 2025 accord that aimed to reduce the number of migrants illegally crossing the Channel to England on small boats, the French interior ministry said on Wednesday.

data.title: Israel-bound plane diverted after co-pilot stabs captain
data.description: JERUSALEM - The co-pilot of a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv tried to crash the plane after stabbing the pilot, but passengers ​then held him ⁠down while other pilots landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday.

data.title: China opens ‘military support centre’ in Laos
data.description: ⁠China has opened ​a new military support and training centre in ​Laos, the Ministry ‌of National Defence said in Beijing as it announced a rare overseas expansion.

data.title: Northern Ireland police probe blockade of divisive parade
data.description: PORTADOWN, Northern Ireland - The police chief of Northern Ireland said Wednesday a criminal probe was under way into protests blocking a pro-British Protestant parade through a mainly Catholic area, as the standoff dragged into a fourth day despite ongoing talks.

data.title: Israel-bound plane diverted after cockpit stabbing
data.description: JERUSALEM - The co-pilot ‌of a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv is believed to have stabbed the captain in a possible attempted “terror attack” on Wednesday, forcing the plane to divert to Saudi Arabia where it landed safely, three Israeli officials said.

data.title: British PM reopens debate on rejoining EU
data.description: LONDON - Andy Burnham put the idea of Britain rejoining the EU on the table on Wednesday, breaking a taboo for a British prime minister and reopening the divisive Brexit debate.

data.title: Russia targets Kyiv power supply as winter approaches
data.description: KYIV - Russia hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure in a wave of deadly drone and missile strikes on Wednesday, prompting an urgent call for civil contingencies as freezing winter approaches.

data.title: ‘Do something,’ begs Iranian woman facing death sentence
data.description: An Iranian woman sentenced to death over protests in Iran earlier this year has begged the international community to save her life and others facing the death penalty, according to an audio message from prison shared by rights groups on Wednesday.

data.title: Israel-bound plane rerouted after cockpit fight
data.description: TABUK, Saudi Arabia - Two pilots were wounded after they reportedly fought on board the plane they were flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv, and which was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.

data.title: Swedish truth commission on Sami people seeks redress
data.description: STOCKHOLM - A Swedish truth commission on Wednesday urged the state to apologise for injustices committed against its indigenous Sami people, including assimilation programmes, and provide compensation and redress.

data.title: Turkey freezes ex-minister's assets as fund crisis grows
data.description: ISTANBUL — Turkish prosecutors have moved to freeze the assets of a top governing party official and former minister who resigned at the weekend over allegations she profited from an investment fund crisis.

data.title: What we know about the North Korean POW dispute
data.description: SEOUL — The transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) from Ukraine to South Korea has sparked a rare public diplomatic row between Seoul and Kyiv.

data.title: Melting ice ‘transforming’ polar ocean habitats
data.description: PARIS - Climate change is increasingly reshaping the polar oceans, with Arctic waters warming rapidly, sea ice shrinking and wildlife losing habitat at both ends of the planet, a report said on Wednesday.
